subject: Re: Clearkite security questionnaire — edge egress & segmentation

Subject: Clearkite Security Questionnaire — edge egress and segmentation

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. We have a tight deadline on the Clearkite security questionnaire — sections are focused on edge egress, network isolation, and threat containment across multi-region inference workloads. The attached checklist highlights the key items we need Redwood to respond to: egress control model, sidecar responsibilities, delta between control plane and data plane, and illustrative attack scenarios (supply chain and host compromise).

Can you confirm whether you can supply a short narrative + a network diagram that shows the recommended Guardrail topology when Redwood is deployed in a customer VPC (private deployment)? Also need the answers formatted for insertion into our RFP doc (spreadsheet attached).

Appreciate a response by EOD Thursday.

Tom
Security Lead
Clearkite Analytics

Attachment: clearkite-egress-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clearkite Security Questionnaire — edge egress and segmentation

Tom — thanks for the checklist. We can provide a concise narrative and a diagram. Draft below is intended for your RFP matrix; I’ve attached a high-level topology SVG and a two-page PDF that explains deployment variants. Highlights:

- Isolation model: Redwood separates the control plane (hosted by Redwood, managed endpoints) from the data plane (customer-managed inference nodes). For Private deployments we offer a customer-controlled data plane that never egresses model inputs to Redwood-hosted storage unless explicitly enabled for telemetry.

- Edge egress controls: By default, inference nodes enforce strict outbound allowlists. We support three egress modes: 1) VPC-only (no internet egress, services reachable via PrivateLink endpoints), 2) Controlled NAT with proxy agent (egress to Redwood-controlled endpoints for optional telemetry), and 3) Customer-managed egress (full customer SOC controls).

- Sidecar responsibilities: A lightweight sidecar runs adjacent to the inference process and mediates all outbound traffic from the container. Sidecar features: mTLS to Redwood endpoints (if enabled), per-request labeling for audit, transparent request batching for cost controls, and an egress policy engine (YAML configured, integrable with your IDP).

- KV cache & token handling: All KV caches on the data plane are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Session tokens are ephemeral, scope-limited, and rotated by the sidecar. No long-term PII is persisted unless explicitly configured by the customer.

- Threat scenarios and mitigations (summary):
  * Host compromise: Sidecar enforces process-level network namespace separation; telemetry is delivered over authenticated channels; we provide a playbook for isolating impacted nodes and rotating keys.
  * Lateral movement: Network ACLs + strict service account scoping; per-route firewall rules and optional host-based IDS integrations.
  * Supply-chain risk (model binaries): Model checksums and provenance metadata are verified in a signed registry; customers can opt for an offline verification step during model deployment.

I’ve included the attached network diagram (network-diagram.svg) showing a recommended VPC layout with Redundancy zones, PrivateLink endpoints for control plane communications, dedicated egress NAT instances with a sidecar-proxy chain, and optional bastionless administrative access via customer IAM roles.

If that covers the checklist items, we’ll format the answers into the spreadsheet rows and send a final package. Karthik — could you review the threat scenarios and confirm the wording on KV cache encryption? Marissa — can you confirm whether the diagram granularity is appropriate for procurement?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Network Assurance
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-deployment-zones.pdf (application/pdf, 216KB)
- network-diagram.svg (image/svg+xml, 164KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clearkite Security Questionnaire — edge egress and segmentation (threat details)

Vanessa — quick pass on the threat wording below. I made two clarifications and one addition:

1) KV cache encryption: confirm that customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments. Add: "Keys can be rotated on a schedule; we provide automation templates (Terraform/Ansible) to rotate KV encryption keys without restarting inference nodes."

2) Sidecar trust boundary: we should call out that the sidecar enforces transport-level authentication for outbound collectors and only permits TLS connections validated against Redwood's mTLS CA or the customer's CA (for fully private setups).

3) Addition — Model rollback & fallback: when an inference host loses access to the primary model registry or detects checksum mismatch, it will automatically switch to a local pinned fallback model variant (read-only) with a configured TTL and emit an elevated audit event; network egress for model fetching is denied until operator intervention. This reduces supply-chain risk and preserves uptime.

I recommend we add two short attack narratives into the RFP response: (A) "Compromised build artifact" — describe detection by mismatch and automated fallback, and (B) "Stolen API key used from within VPC" — describe per-request signing & short-lived tokens mitigations. I attached a one-page mitigation table for insertion.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation-table-onepager.txt (text/plain, 9KB)

Tom — attaching the finalized responses and the diagram. We formatted the answers to match your spreadsheet columns and included short narrative attack scenarios with mitigations. Key callouts for Clearkite:

- For a fully private deployment we recommend: PrivateLink control plane, VPC-only egress (no internet NAT), sidecar-enforced allowlists, and customer-managed KMS for KV encryption.
- If you need telemetry to Redwood, use the Controlled NAT mode with mutual TLS and an allowlist of Redwood ingest endpoints; telemetry is optional and toggled per-customer.
- We include an automated model-fallback mechanism and signed model registries to mitigate supply-chain risk.
